mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals a loosening of monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the market, boosting investor confidence and driving up S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS decreases by > 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) indicates strong consumer demand, which is a leading indicator of corporate earnings growth and thus positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where RSAFS increases by > 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a tightening labor market, which typically leads to wage inflation and increased consumer spending, driving up S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE decreases.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a strong supply side of the economy, which is a positive signal for corporate earnings and thus S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where INDPRO increases by > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 2% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to monetary tightening and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increases by > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL increases by > 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises by more than 0.5% and nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) decrease by more than 100,000 in a month, it signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by > 0.5% and PAYEMS decreases by > 100,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE increases by > 0.5% and PAYEMS decreases by > 100,000.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals strong demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and thus positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 50% of instances where HOUST increases by > 5%.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) decreases by more than 1% and real GDP (GDPC1) growth is negative in the same quarter, it signals a contraction in the supply side of the economy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by > 1% and GDPC1 growth is negative
failure_condition: S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where INDPRO decreases by > 1% and GDPC1 growth is negative.
